approach: The wave speed is the ratio of the angular frequency to the wave number, read directly from the coefficients of t and x.

steps.text: Identify the wave number and the angular frequency from the equation.
steps.equation: y = 0.02 sin(πx − 8πt), so k = π rad m⁻¹, ω = 8π rad s⁻¹

steps.text: Find the wave speed from the ratio of angular frequency to wave number.

common_mistakes.text: Computing the frequency f = ω/2π = 4 Hz and the wavelength λ = 2π/k = 2 m correctly, then doubling the product to get v = 2fλ = 16 ms⁻¹.
Dividing the wave number by the angular frequency instead of the other way round, giving v = π/8π = 0.125 ms⁻¹, which matches no option.
